records.region: Northwestern San Luis; western Sierra de San Luis to Pampa de las Salinas
records.material_pending_reason: The southern westward opening and subsequent northward transfer into the depicted collector are not established by the two regional originals. The final selected continuation inside Pampa de las Salinas has a supported salt-flat setting but no independently traced through-going channel. Regional basin membership, neighboring Nogolí drainage and aqueduct imports do not fill these gaps.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The mapped northward collector approaching Pampa de las Salinas. The southern opening, its transfer into this collector and the final within-salina continuation are excluded.
records.completion_scope: All 42 selected parts were considered. Two independently issued originals establish the middle/northern drainage setting, a Bajo Retamo collector candidate and the Pampa de las Salinas receiving setting. The southern connector and internal terminal passage remain substantive correspondence gaps, so this is not a completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: IGN writes R. del Bajo Retamo; the independent provincial study labels Río de Bajo Retamo. Its prose also describes Cañada de Vilance as the basin collector. This does not establish that every selected reach carries any one of these names.

scope_limits: The first selected watercourse is unnamed in this finding; it is not automatically Río Nogolí.
The source gap concerns an actual southern connection and an internal terminal passage, not a demand for exact banks or one uniform name.
The middle/northern collector candidate does not establish a representative identity for the complete modeled group.
Source epochs and regional scale do not establish current hydraulic behavior or managed-operation status.

records.region: Amacuro river corridor in the northeastern Venezuela–Guyana border region, from the Imataca upland setting toward the coastal waters southwest of the separate Barima outlet. Geographic wording records the source locations and does not adopt a position on territorial sovereignty or a legal boundary.
records.candidate_name_role: Supported regional river-corridor candidate, with historical Amakura spelling corroborated by the State Department study. It is not a completed representative identity for all five selected fragments and does not assign that name to every feeder or connector.
records.material_pending_reason: No acquired primary cartography establishes the full chosen southwestern headward route through fragments 11254–11255, the northward middle connection in 11256, or all joins and channel distinctions around the eastern bend in 11257. Figure14 is a generalized functional-geography map whose thematic text and arrows partly obscure lower drainage. IBS21 contains a historical point list and prose, not a continuous map. These are substantive source-to-route gaps, rather than merely an unknown small-stream name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection approaches northeast from the southwestern upland, continues east, turns north and briefly northeast, then bends northwest to its own coastal opening. It is not the long Barima corridor, the separate Mora Passage or the Waini estuary studied for another target. The modeled route and length do not define a legal boundary, natural source or official river length.
records.completion_scope: Every selected fragment, all four inter-fragment joins and the actual last endpoint were considered against the acquired regional map and relevant prose. Lower coastal correspondence is visible at ordinary regional scale. The complete southwestern opening, eastward upper connector and middle through-links are not established; thematic labels also interrupt the lower-map linework. Geographic name anchors and nearby river labels are not substituted for these missing links.
records.supported_name_scope: The authored Delta Amacuro chapter expressly distinguishes Río Amacuro, giving access to San José de Amacuro, from Barima and the Arature and Basama waterways. Its thematic cartography supports the lower northwestward waterway and coastal opening. The independent historical study names Amacuro and its Haiowa junction and supplies named upper-river landmarks, without mapping the complete selected channel.

scope_limits: Full selected upper and middle channel correspondence remains unresolved despite a strong regional Amacuro association.
The modeled five-fragment mainstem roles do not name all natural feeder channels or establish hydronym boundaries.
The historical survey landmarks are contextual name anchors, not a substitute for an inspected continuous river map.
The lower thematic map is partly obscured; the separately visible terminal setting does not complete the upstream through-links.
No current hydraulic connection, current wetland condition, exact bank, official source/mouth, formal naming date or legal territorial boundary is established.
The fixed modeled length is not an official Río Amacuro length.

records.region: Comondú, Baja California Sur, Mexico; eastern mountain feeder through the Las Bramonas plain corridor to the lagoon-side coast near Puerto Adolfo López Mateos.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Arroyo Las Bramonas is supported as the receiving main-corridor and representative connected-system identity. The chosen eastern feeder remains individually unnamed here, and San Gregorio is retained as the upper-reach name used by the 2019 integrated study. Neither is made a blanket alias or whole-object scalar.
records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary-scale geographic correspondence for the entire one-fragment selection, including the chosen eastern feeder, all 24 parts and joins, desert/plain reaches, and the final lagoon-side inlet. A representative Las Bramonas identity is supported without requiring one name for every component or precise bank, source-point, confluence or tidal-boundary vertices.
records.supported_name_scope: Arroyo Las Bramonas is supported as the receiving main-corridor and representative connected-system identity. The chosen eastern feeder remains individually unnamed here, and San Gregorio is retained as the upper-reach name used by the 2019 integrated study. Neither is made a blanket alias or whole-object scalar.

naming_scope_details.coastal_receiver_scope: Lagoon-side inlet beside Puerto Adolfo López Mateos, landward of Isla Magdalena; no more specific inlet hydronym assigned.
naming_scope_details.source_label_difference: The 2019 study labels the selected upper valley San Gregorio and describes it as a Las Bramonas tributary. The generalized 2010 municipal map places Las Bramonas along the broader upper corridor. These are preserved as source-specific scopes, not proof of exact aliases or name-change vertices.
naming_scope_details.reservoir_and_managed_passages: No mapped large reservoir crossing is required along the selected route. The report locates El Ihuajil on the separate San Luis tributary and another named Las Bramonas dam on the San José de la Noria approach; their names are not transferred to the chosen San Gregorio passage. Agricultural terrain does not alone establish canal status.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The modeled length and sea-terminal attribute are not evidence of surveyed river length, present discharge, perennial water, current shoreline or current reservoir operations.

bounded_name_observations.scope: Separately named upper reach in the2019 integrated study; not a whole-system alias

records.region: Southern Bahia/northern Espírito Santo border region and Atlantic coastal setting
records.material_pending_reason: No proposed primary original supplied usable map or substantive river-corridor prose. The opening, every intervening connection, lower wetland/estuarine setting and actual sea terminal all remain source-material pending.
records.completion_scope: The bounded source pass is finished and all 35 selected parts were considered for coverage; no component is asserted to have completed geographic correspondence. This is a genuine source-material gap, not a completed naming-scope hold.

scope_limits: The selected river identity is not established by the catalogue or discovery-only names.
No component has usable original-source geographic correspondence.
The model sea-terminal class does not prove the actual coastward through-link.
The AGERH original request terminal HTTP/body outcome is unknown and no partial output was read.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
